where: blaze: a proc-macro crate built as two units (Lowered::macros)
what: A proc-macro crate that a build plans twice (two profiles: `misses` cause `twice`, key parts `plan` and `profile` differ; 22 of reth's units) is one crate in the front end, and each unit gave the crate its expanders as it ended: the crate had the module of whichever unit ended last, `ProcMacros` was written once or twice in every build with nothing changed, and the order differed from build to build (events `a proc-macro crate's expanders loaded`: runs 2d62a1037d and 438aa907e9 in turn).
cost: found only after the first fix left one write per build on a three-crate fixture
cause: two values (two modules) under one key (the front end's crate), the last writer winning
whys: why written: the crate's expanders were replaced each build
why: two units load two modules for one crate
why two: the plan builds the crate under two profiles and the front end has one crate per package target
why undetected: nothing refuses a second, different value for a crate's expanders in one build (rule keys-cover-every-input)
property: a front-end input keyed by crate is fed by units keyed by crate and profile
class: two values under one key decided by timing: an input whose writers are more finely keyed than it is
prevention: built (6fd7961cf9): `ProcMacroExpander::replaces`: the same code built into another module replaces the held one only when its module is the lesser, so the crate's expanders are a function of the build. Not built: the same for a build script's run classes is there already (`applies_for_class`); a general refusal when two units of one build give one crate different inputs is open
fix: 6fd7961cf9: the fixture's third build writes 0 inputs, runs 0 rows
